content.text:
I fixed it: request bodies are now unlimited by default whether or not redirects are on, as the issue asks.

**Cause:** axios's default `maxBodyLength` is `-1`, meaning unlimited. The Node HTTP adapter only passed the option on to `follow-redirects` when it was above `-1`. So by default, `follow-redirects` used its own hidden 10MB limit. With `maxRedirects: 0` that library isn't used at all, which is why there was no limit in that case.

**Fix** (`lib/adapters/http.js`): when `maxBodyLength` is `-1`, the adapter now passes `Infinity` to `follow-redirects`. I also added a line in `README.md` saying the default is `-1` (unlimited) regardless of `maxRedirects`.

**Checked against a local server with a 20MB body:**

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| default | OK (failed with the 10MB error before) |
| `maxBodyLength: -1` | OK |
| `maxRedirects: 0` | OK |
| `maxBodyLength: 100` | "Request body larger than maxBodyLength limit" (limit still enforced) |

**Tests:** in `test/unit/adapters/http.js`, 56 pass and 1 fails ("should support max content length", which gets a 400 status instead of the expected error). That test fails the same way with my change removed, so it isn't caused by this fix.
